sentences.text:
In The High Court At Calcutta
21-02-2023
Criminal Miscellaneous Jurisdiction Item no.02 Appellate Side bail allowed Crm (Sb) 35 of 2023

In Re: An application for bail under Section 439 of the code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 filed on 15th February, 2023 in connection with in connection with Chapra Police Station Case No. 723 of 2022 dated 24.12.2022 under Sections 420/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
Mr. Arijit Ganguly Mr. Kousik Kundu ... for the State.

Mr. Majumdar, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody for 44 days and the case being based on documents, further detention may not be warranted.
Learned advocate prays that on any condition the petitioner may be released on bail.
Mr. Ganguly, learned advocate appearing for the State opposes the prayer for bail and draws the attention of the court to the relevant pages of the case diary.
Learned advocate also filed Memorandum of Evidence, let the same be kept with the record.

I have considered the merits of the case and is of the opinion that a case has been made out, but the detention of the petitioner may not be warranted further in the present circumstances available before this court.

Accordingly, the petitioner shall be released on bail by furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/-(Rupees ten thousand only) with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, subject to the satisfaction of the Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Krishnagar, Nadia.
If on bail, the petitioner shall meet with the Investigating Officer once in a week till further orders of this court.
Petitioner shall inform his address/place of residence to the learned C.J.M, Nadia as well as the Investigating Officer and any change thereof should be immediately informed to both the authorities.

Any violation of the aforesaid conditions would entitle the learned C.J.M, Nadia to cancel the bail with further reference to this court.
